article_title: Neural signals gradually shift towards inferior frontal gyrus and long-term effects following facial imitation-based social learning
citation: Qi Liu, Siyu Zhu, Can Liu, Yanmiao Yang, Chunmei Lan, Xinwei Song, Benjamin Becker, Keith M. Kendrick, Xinqi Zhou & Weihua Zhao. (2025). Neural signals gradually shift towards inferior frontal gyrus and long-term effects following facial imitation-based social learning. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00372-9
title: Mirror neuron system information-flow account of imitation-based social learning
description: The article proposes that facial imitation-based social learning is supported by the mirror neuron system (IFG, IPL, STS), whose representational pathway reorganizes with practice: early and middle phases show bidirectional IFG–IPL, IPL–STS and STS–IFG coupling, but "by the end of the period of repetitive FISL course, the main ﬂow of representational information was directed from the IPL/STS to the IFG". The IFG is described as taking a dominant role, receiving increased sensory or visual input that lets it flexibly execute imitation goals with greater accuracy or speed. The account also holds that refined, more similar MNS representations and strengthened MNS connectivity with social-cognition regions underlie improved imitation and face-emotion perception.
requirements: Repeated imitative learning practice over multiple sessions for the representational reorganization to emerge
Neuroimaging (fNIRS/fMRI) to observe the spatiotemporal trajectory of MNS changes
constraints: Findings from male participants only; the authors state they cannot extrapolate to females
fNIRS covered only the three main cortical MNS regions, not premotor or supplementary motor regions
Deliberate conscious imitation was trained, so unconscious motor contagion contributions cannot be ruled out
target_learners: Individuals with social-cognition deficits (e.g., ASD, schizophrenia, depression), as proposed clinical applications
target_learning_goals: Imitative accuracy and speed for facial expressions
Recognition and perception of others' emotional facial expressions
examples: Eighty male participants imitated 20 validated facial expressions across 16 sessions over one month, with fNIRS in the 2nd, 9th and 16th sessions and pre/post fMRI face and scene perception tasks
key_sources: Qi Liu, Siyu Zhu, Can Liu, Yanmiao Yang, Chunmei Lan, Xinwei Song, Benjamin Becker, Keith M. Kendrick, Xinqi Zhou & Weihua Zhao. (2025). Neural signals gradually shift towards inferior frontal gyrus and long-term effects following facial imitation-based social learning. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00372-9

article_title: The Impact of Musical Mnemonic on Vocabulary Recalling of Iranian Young Learners
citation: Bahrami, Z. N., Izadpanah, S. & Bijani, H. (2019). The Impact of Musical Mnemonic on Vocabulary Recalling of Iranian Young Learners. International Journal of Instruction, 12(1), 977-994. http://www.e-iji.net
title: Mnemonics as memory-enhancement devices that speed learning by linking new information to familiar structures
description: The article defines mnemonics as memory devices and recall aids that help learners remember information, tracing the term to the Greek "Mnemosyne". Citing Amiryousefi and Ketabi, it holds that mnemonics are "an improvement technique or memory enhancement device which aid information processing including encoding, storage, and recall in memory" and that they speed learning by incorporating new information into cognitive and intellectual units, connecting new information with old familiar information using pictures, words, letters, or combinations of them. The study instantiates this account with music as the mnemonic device.
requirements: New information must be connected to old familiar information (here, a familiar melody) for the mnemonic to aid encoding and recall
constraints: The account is presented as background theory drawn from cited prior work rather than tested directly in this study
target_learners: language learners of all ages learning vocabulary
target_learning_goals: memory for new vocabulary: encoding, storage, and recall
examples: The study's musical group rehearsed a sung word list across four recall trials, operationalizing mnemonic encoding, storage and recall through melody and rhythm
key_sources: Bahrami, Z. N., Izadpanah, S. & Bijani, H. (2019). The Impact of Musical Mnemonic on Vocabulary Recalling of Iranian Young Learners. International Journal of Instruction, 12(1), 977-994. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1201149
